section.heading: Definitions.

para.text: For the purposes of this subchapter, the term:
"Direct support" means behavioral health crises assessment and intervention services.

"High-need area" means a defined geographic area, which may include a neighborhood, corridor, or cluster of blocks, designated by the Department as experiencing a disproportionately high concentration of substance use disorder activity, including opioid use, overdoses, or related behavioral health service needs, based on available public health data, service utilization data, or other relevant indicators.

"Relationship development" means regular interactions, and the incorporation of peer supports, when possible, that foster open communications and encourage active engagement with behavioral health services for individuals using substances.

"Resource brokering" means assistance with accessing supportive services and public benefits, including housing, food, Medicaid, Social Security Income or Social Security Disability Insurance, and transportation services needed to access primary and behavioral health care.

section.codify:annotation: Applicability of D.C. Law 26-142: § 3 of D.C. Law 26-142 provided that the creation of this section by § 2 of D.C. Law 26-142 is subject to the inclusion of the law’s fiscal effect in an approved budget and financial plan. Therefore that amendment has not been implemented.
